chapters.title: Why a pyramid structure
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 1 explains why pyramid structure reduces reader burden: the higher point summarizes grouped support, groups must be logical, and communication runs top-down only after bottom-up thinking has earned the answer.
chapters.coreMove: Earn the answer through bottom-up grouping, then lead with it so the reader can judge support instead of assembling it.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the pyramid as a faster executive-summary style or a prettier outline instead of a discipline for deciding what the support adds up to.

chapters.title: The substructures within the pyramid
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 2 narrows from why pyramids help to what makes the internal substructure stable: the point above must summarize, siblings must be logically alike, and sibling order must mean something.
chapters.coreMove: Test every support set for vertical summary, horizontal sameness, and meaningful order before trusting the hierarchy.
chapters.commonMisread: Assuming parallel bullets or matching grammar make a real group when the lower points are doing different jobs.

chapters.title: How to build a pyramid structure
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 3 is construction discipline: bottom-up approach, caveats for beginners, grouping raw material, ordering it, and letting the higher-order idea emerge before top-down delivery.
chapters.coreMove: Build the hierarchy from raw material upward, letting classification and order create the top sentence instead of forcing a headline early.
chapters.commonMisread: Starting with a confident top line and hunting for support afterward.

chapters.title: Fine points of introductions
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 4 focuses on introductions: introductory flow, length, where to start the situation, what counts as complication, why that order, key-line timing, and patterns such as requests for funds, how-to documents, proposals, progress reviews, transitions, and summaries.
chapters.coreMove: Frame situation, complication, and the active reader question before releasing the key line.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating introductions as throat-clearing, scene-setting, or a place to hide the answer until the reader is patient enough.

chapters.title: Deduction and induction: the difference
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 5 distinguishes deduction and induction, how each works, when to use each, and how inductive reasoning differs inside pyramid logic.
chapters.coreMove: Choose the reasoning motion the material can honestly carry: linked chain for deduction, parallel pattern for induction.
chapters.commonMisread: Using deduction and induction as impressive labels while mixing chain logic and sibling logic in the same support set.

chapters.title: How to highlight the structure
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 6 turns to visible presentation: underlined points, decimal numbering, and indented display as ways to expose hierarchy so the reader need not reconstruct it.
chapters.coreMove: Make rank, sequence, and dependence visible on the page without pretending formatting can create logic.
chapters.commonMisread: Believing that numbering, underlining, or indentation will fix a structure that is still vague or mixed.

chapters.title: Questioning the order of a grouping
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 7 questions group order: time order, confused logic, false grouping, structural order, describing versus imposing structure, ranking order, and improper class groupings.
chapters.coreMove: Name and test the ordering rule of a group, then reject sequences and classes the material cannot honestly support.
chapters.commonMisread: Choosing an order that feels tidy, familiar, or persuasive without proving it belongs to the material.

chapters.title: Questioning the problem-solving process
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 8 moves upstream to problem solving: what the problem is, why it exists, what to do about it, period graph books, structuring analysis of the problem, and the logic-tree concept.
chapters.coreMove: Separate problem definition, diagnosis, and action, then structure the inquiry before trusting the recommendation.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the visible symptom or preferred fix as the problem and then organizing a recommendation around that shortcut.
mustUseTerms: what should we do about it

chapters.title: Questioning the summary statement
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 9 tests the summary statement: stating action effects, making wording specific, distinguishing levels of action, drawing inference from conclusions, finding structural similarity, and visualizing relationships.
chapters.coreMove: Make the summary line specific, level-accurate, and structurally faithful to the conclusions beneath it.
chapters.commonMisread: Writing a polished headline that sounds strategic while overclaiming, underclaiming, or blurring what the lower points prove.

chapters.title: Putting it into readable words
chapters.sourcePressure: Chapter 10 closes by putting structure into readable words: create the image first, then copy the image in words, keeping readability accountable to the structure it carries.
chapters.coreMove: Translate the already-earned structure into sentences that preserve its image instead of smoothing it into blur.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating readability as pleasant phrasing, simplification, or style polish after the thinking is done.
